paragraphs.text: translated by
1. THIS very thing ye Twain hold as your object: ye weave your songs as skillful men weave garments.
paragraphs.original: उभा उ नूनं तदिदर्थयेथे वि तन्वाथे धियो वस्त्रापसेव ।
paragraphs.translit: ubhā u nūnaṃ tadidarthayethe vi tanvāthe dhiyo vastrāpaseva |

paragraphs.text: That ye may come united have I waked you: ye spread out food like days of lovely weather.
paragraphs.original: सध्रीचीना यातवे प्रेमजीगः सुदिनेव पृक्ष आ तंसयेथे
paragraphs.translit: sadhrīcīnā yātave premajīgaḥ sudineva pṛkṣa ā taṃsayethe

paragraphs.text: 2. Like two plough-bulls ye move along in traces, and seek like eager guests your bidder's banquet.
paragraphs.original: उष्टारेव फर्वरेषु श्रयेथे प्रायोगेव श्वात्र्या शासुरेथः ।
paragraphs.translit: uṣṭāreva pharvareṣu śrayethe prāyogeva śvātryā śāsurethaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Ye are like glorious envoys mid the people: like bulls, approach the place where ye are watered.
paragraphs.original: दूतेव हि ष्ठो यशसा जनेषु माप स्थातं महिषेवावपानात्
paragraphs.translit: dūteva hi ṣṭho yaśasā janeṣu māpa sthātaṃ mahiṣevāvapānāt

paragraphs.text: 3. Like the two pinions of a bird, connected, like two choice animals, ye have sought our worship.
paragraphs.original: साकंयुजा शकुनस्येव पक्षा पश्वेव चित्रा यजुरा गमिष्टम् ।
paragraphs.translit: sākaṃyujā śakunasyeva pakṣā paśveva citrā yajurā gamiṣṭam |

paragraphs.text: Bright as the fire the votary hath kindled, ye sacrifice in many a spot as roamers.
4. Ye are our kinsmen, like two sons, two fathers, strong in your splendour and like kings for conquest;
paragraphs.original: आपी वो अस्मे पितरेव पुत्रोग्रेव रुचा नृपतीव तुर्यै ।
paragraphs.translit: āpī vo asme pitareva putrogreva rucā nṛpatīva turyai |

paragraphs.text: Like rays for our enjoyment, Lords to feed us, ye, like quick bearers, have obeyed our calling.
paragraphs.original: इर्येव पुष्ट्यै किरणेव भुज्यै श्रुष्टीवानेव हवमा गमिष्टम्
paragraphs.translit: iryeva puṣṭyai kiraṇeva bhujyai śruṣṭīvāneva havamā gamiṣṭam

paragraphs.text: 5. You are like two pleasantly moving well-fed (hills) like Mitra and Varuna,
paragraphs.original: वंसगेव पूषर्या शिम्बाता मित्रेव ऋता शतरा शातपन्ता । वाजेवोच्चा वयसा घर्म्येष्ठा मेषेवेषा सपर्या पुरीषा
paragraphs.translit: vaṃsageva pūṣaryā śimbātā mitreva ṛtā śatarā śātapantā | vājevoccā vayasā gharmyeṣṭhā meṣeveṣā saparyā purīṣā

paragraphs.text: the two bestowers of felicity, veracious, possessors of infinite wealth, happy,
like two horses plump with fodder, abiding in the firmament,
like two rams (are you) to be nourished with sacrificial food, to be cherished (with oblations).
6. You are like two mad elephants bending their forequarters and smiting the foe,
paragraphs.original: सृण्येव जर्भरी तुर्फरीतू नैतोशेव तुर्फरी पर्फरीका । उदन्यजेव जेमना मदेरू ता मे जराय्वजरं मरायु
paragraphs.translit: sṛṇyeva jarbharī turpharītū naitośeva turpharī parpharīkā | udanyajeva jemanā maderū tā me jarāyvajaraṃ marāyu

paragraphs.text: like the two sons of Nitosa destroying (foes),
and cherishing (friends); you are bright as two water-born (jewels),
do you, who are victorious, (render) my decaying mortal body free from decay.
7. Fierce (Asvins), like two powerful (heroes), you enable this moving,
paragraphs.original: पज्रेव चर्चरं जारं मरायु क्षद्मेवार्थेषु तर्तरीथ उग्रा । ऋभू नापत्खरमज्रा खरज्रुर्वायुर्न पर्फरत्क्षयद्रयीणाम्
paragraphs.translit: pajreva carcaraṃ jāraṃ marāyu kṣadmevārtheṣu tartarītha ugrā | ṛbhū nāpatkharamajrā kharajrurvāyurna parpharatkṣayadrayīṇām

paragraphs.text: perishable mortal (frame) to cross over to the objects (of its destination) as over water;
extremely strong, like the Rbhus, your chariot, attained its destination swift as the wind,
it pervaded (everywhere), it dispensed riches.
8. With your bellies full of the Soma, like two saucepans, preservers of wealth, destroyers of enemies.
paragraphs.original: घर्मेव मधु जठरे सनेरू भगेविता तुर्फरी फारिवारम् । पतरेव चचरा चन्द्रनिर्णिङ्मनऋङ्गा मनन्या न जग्मी
paragraphs.translit: gharmeva madhu jaṭhare sanerū bhagevitā turpharī phārivāram | patareva cacarā candranirṇiṅmanaṛṅgā mananyā na jagmī

paragraphs.text: (you are) armed with hatchets, moving like two flying (birds)
with forms like the moon, attaining success through the mind, like two laudable beings,
(you are) approaching (the sacrifice).
9. Like giants, ye will find firm ground to stand on in depths, like feet for one who fords a shallow.
paragraphs.original: बृहन्तेव गम्भरेषु प्रतिष्ठां पादेव गाधं तरते विदाथः ।
paragraphs.translit: bṛhanteva gambhareṣu pratiṣṭhāṃ pādeva gādhaṃ tarate vidāthaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Like cars ye will attend to him who orders: ye Two enjoy our wondrous work as sharers.
paragraphs.original: कर्णेव शासुरनु हि स्मराथोऽंशेव नो भजतं चित्रमप्नः
paragraphs.translit: karṇeva śāsuranu hi smarātho'ṃśeva no bhajataṃ citramapnaḥ

paragraphs.text: 10. Like toiling bees ye bring to us your honey, as bees into the hide that opens downward.
paragraphs.original: आरङ्गरेव मध्वेरयेथे सारघेव गवि नीचीनबारे । कीनारेव स्वेदमासिष्विदाना क्षामेवोर्जा सूयवसात्सचेथे
paragraphs.translit: āraṅgareva madhverayethe sāragheva gavi nīcīnabāre | kīnāreva svedamāsiṣvidānā kṣāmevorjā sūyavasātsacethe

paragraphs.text: 11. May we increase the laud and gain us vigour: come to our song, ye whom one chariot carries.
paragraphs.original: ऋध्याम स्तोमं सनुयाम वाजमा नो मन्त्रं सरथेहोप यातम् ।
paragraphs.translit: ṛdhyāma stomaṃ sanuyāma vājamā no mantraṃ sarathehopa yātam |

paragraphs.text: Filled be our kine with ripened meath like glory: Bhutamsa hath fulfilled the Asvins' longing.
paragraphs.original: यशो न पक्वं मधु गोष्वन्तरा भूतांशो अश्विनोः काममप्राः
paragraphs.translit: yaśo na pakvaṃ madhu goṣvantarā bhūtāṃśo aśvinoḥ kāmamaprāḥ
